blocks.tamil_translation: forgiven. A man committed a sin at night. Even though Allah Ta'ala had concealed his sin (so that people would not know of it), the next morning he made it public, saying, “Friend! Last night I did such-and-such (sinful) things.” Making public a sinful act that was concealed also counts as sinning openly. He spent the night with his Lord having concealed the wrong he did. In the morning he removed the veil that Allah Ta'ala had placed over his sin (in the night),” Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: اِذَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ: هَلَكَ النَّاسُ فَهُوَ اَهْلَكُهُمْ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم، باب النهي عن قول هلك الناس، رقم: ٦٦٨٣
blocks.tamil_translation: “Whoever says, “The people are ruined,” it is he who will be ruined more than all the people.” (Because the one who says this, by regarding others as lowly, has fallen into the sin of pride.) Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ﵁ قَالَ: تُوُفِّيَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ اَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ يَعْنِيْ رَجُلاً:اَبْشِرْ بِالْجَنَّةِ، فَقَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: اَوَ لَا تَدْرِيْ، فَلَعَلَّهُ تَكَلَّمَ فِيْمَا لَا يَعْنِيْهِ اَوْ بَخِلَ بِمَا لَا يَنْقُصُهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال: هذا حسن غريب، باب حديث من حسن اسلام المرء....رقم:٢٣١٦
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrates that a Sahabi passed away. A man (looking at the deceased) said, “I give you the good news that you will get Jannah.” “How can you say this without knowing the true state of affairs? This man may have spoken some useless word
